feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows broad leadership across platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. Impact is solid but could be sharper with more outcome-focused metrics and tighter consolidation of repeated skills/sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior brand: the headline, summary, and role progression consistently support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility and scope: large-scale website migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search work all signal substantive ownership.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with strong action verbs and relevant technical specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, search performance, campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; this will improve structure and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Minor style/consistency edits: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; consider consistent capitalization styling for the name (“Coleman Davis” vs “Coleman DAVIS”). No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground scale/outcomes: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading enterprise web modernization and communications systems for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with simpler, more direct phrasing like “leading the platforms, governance, and content operations that power.”
- Consider adding one concrete signal of scope from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Refine the second sentence to emphasize current relevance: “Combines platform strategy, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search to improve discovery, governance, and delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies/footer; “AI-enabled search” would be more specific and distinctive.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” echoes multiple skills sections; keep the intro sharper and less list-like.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner scanning.
- Replace “communications operations” with a more senior framing like “communications strategy and operations.”
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications strategy and operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, drop one lower-priority item such as “livestream operations” or combine it into “multimedia production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeat language already used in the header and recent projects.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Workflow automation and platform integration” also overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps heavily with the NACo experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinctiveness would make it more valuable as a footer.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with sharper ones and add outcome/context where possible: audience, scale, campaign purpose, or business impact.
- Standardize style: use either sentence case or title case consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat recent NACo experience bullets.
- If space is tight, keep only projects not already clearly covered in Work Experience or add distinct results not mentioned elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, recent strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with positioning: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into 3–4 impact bullets focused on consulting outcomes: governance/workflows, campaign/microsite delivery, technical implementation, AI search strategy.
- Replace generic phrases like “build and refine” / “advise on best practices” with stronger verbs: “designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “defined.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance/usability best practices” repeat themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsite and AI search details duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor achievement; keep the metrics and add outcome language if possible: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize scale or performance, not just oversight; add open rates, audience growth, engagement, or campaign results if available.
- Combine operations/governance/analytics into one impact-focused bullet: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing publishing standards and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless this role emphasizes the studio build and expanded capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or process improvements achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting organization-wide advocacy and editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: newsletter open/click growth, video cadence/views, publishing turnaround time, stakeholder/team count, or workflow efficiency gains.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this only if you can quantify how this role scaled it.
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 governance bullet; frame this as earlier-stage operational buildout.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and heavily overlaps with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the highest-value leadership strengths and use wording that reflects recent enterprise-scale work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal language tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise web strategy & modernization
- Editorial governance & publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & member communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications leadership” for concision.
- Change “Audience-focused content planning” to “Audience-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- If space allows, align one phrase to measurable scale from recent roles, e.g., “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; vary the phrasing or cut one.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the most recent/high-value work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long stack list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress only if it is still relevant to target roles; it is not supported by recent experience.
- Replace “technical execution” filler with stronger outcome-oriented phrasing where possible, e.g., “enterprise CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences.”
- If space allows, add one scale cue aligned to recent work elsewhere, such as “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Most tools repeat the Technical + IT section; Topline Skills should be more curated than exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and business impact more than platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a pure software inventory.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: “Measurement strategy,” “dashboarding and executive insights,” or “conversion/performance optimization” if accurate.
- Suggested rewrite: “Measurement strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they are already listed below; Topline Skills should signal senior-level capability, not inventory.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific, tool-/environment-oriented, and avoid repeating broad “video/livestream” language already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward delivery capability, not generic functions: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera operation and switching • Video editing and post-production • Virtual event technical coordination”
- If accurate, add tools/platforms to increase credibility: “Premiere Pro, Audition, PTZ workflows, livestream studio environments”
- Replace “Studio operations” with a clearer outcome-oriented phrase like “In-house studio production” or “Broadcast studio setup and operation”
- Keep this section concise; let work experience carry impact claims such as building NACo’s in-house studio and producing recurring advocacy video

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” is close to project/work-history evidence; avoid repeating full claims here

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be more specific about level/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating stronger skills elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize primary vs secondary platforms: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency cues tied to recent work: **Drupal (lead platform; migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms** for clarity and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If GitHub Pages was only lightly used, remove it and keep the list tighter and more senior-relevant.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed version there and shortening this item.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent experience, so avoid repeating it without added context or differentiation.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation tools that support recent delivery, not repeat broader platform skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something tighter and more senior: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with a more execution-focused list: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows**
- Standardize phrasing for clarity and professionalism: use **REST/API integrations** instead of just “API integrations,” and **GitHub Actions/CI workflows** to show practical application.
- If space allows, add one brief qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **used for Drupal front-end delivery, tagging, automation and lightweight edge scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- Consider whether **Google Tag Manager** belongs here or under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** to reduce category blur.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more selective and signal how these tools were used to improve operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add light context instead of pure listing: **Used to build editorial planning systems, automate cross-team workflows, and support project coordination**
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools; drop weaker or less central platforms if not used meaningfully in recent roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Airtable systems** and **Workflow automation** already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis verbatim
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar PM tools; listing all four can look unfocused unless each was used substantially

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal enterprise-scale email operations. Because recent roles emphasize email leadership, this should reflect platform depth, not just list names.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email newsletter operations”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier: “member communications, newsletter distribution, audience engagement”
- Keep platform naming consistent and concise; consider shortening to “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights” unless “Journeys” is specifically important to the roles targeted.
- Order by strongest/recent relevance: put Higher Logic first if it was the primary NACo platform; otherwise keep Dynamics 365 first for enterprise weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications claims elsewhere; avoid adding generic phrases like “social/email engagement.”
- Don’t repeat audience scale here if it’s already covered in recent NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, tie it to the recent NACo analytics buildout.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboards**
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with **KPI dashboards** or **executive reporting dashboards** to show business use.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work, e.g., “supported reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep one detailed version and make the other shorter or broader.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are fine here, but avoid repeating them in multiple skills sections unless backed by outcomes.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific scope/results where possible: website refresh size, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Possible full rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later operations/governance themes; keep this lighter here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia work. Emphasize the launch/ownership angle and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, project coordination and digital communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a tighter, more active line such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director roles; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid repeating “weekly video” or broader digital operations here, since those are stronger in more recent roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently a mix of software and capabilities and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to named tools only, or make the capabilities more specific and outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit:
